# Japan Equities & Macro Briefing — 5 November 2026

Tokyo opens after a violent risk-off session. The Nikkei fell more than 3,000 yen as investors feared the US Democratic midterm landslide ("Blue Tsunami") would bring tighter AI and data-center regulation, compounded by a CoreWeave-led selloff in AI infrastructure. Overnight, Wall Street rotated sharply rather than crashing: the Dow rose as much as 1,500 points on financials and "Trump–Democrat cooperation" hopes, while data-center names sold off. That sets up an expected technical rebound in Tokyo. Domestic corporate news was constructive: trading houses, utilities and shipping raised guidance, Mitsubishi Corporation unveiled a ¥1 trillion buyback, and semiconductor-materials consolidation accelerated with Mitsui Chemicals' bid for JSR. The top implication is to rotate away from crowded AI-capex and data-center beneficiaries toward cash-rich, shareholder-return names. These include trading houses, utilities and shipping, along with domestic financials. Treat the Nikkei rebound as a chance to trim high-beta AI exposure rather than chase it.

## US Midterms & Global Risk Sentiment

- **The Democrats won decisively**, driven by inflation anger and "Trump fatigue." Exit sentiment captured by WSJ, summed up as "I've had enough," points to cost of living as the decisive issue [10][28]. Historically, a divided Washington after midterms (1994, 2010, 2018) produced gridlock that markets tolerated well. The key difference this time is the explicit threat to AI and data-center buildout, which has been the core earnings driver for Japanese semicap and electrical names. Expect US fiscal expansion to stall. That is mildly positive for UST yields, and thus for yen strength at the margin, and negative for policy-driven US capex themes.
- **The US equity reaction was a rotation, not a rout.** The Dow rose as much as 1,500 points intraday as Trump signalled "cooperation with Democrats," and financials led [13][33]. Nikkei notes, however, that the GAFAM highs masked heavy selling in data-center plays [12]. A separate Nikkei column warns that Wall Street's optimism on financials is dangerous because a Democratic House could revive bank regulation [15]. The read-through for Japan is that megabanks with US exposure (MUFG via Morgan Stanley, SMFG via Jefferies) may get a sentiment lift. Treat it as tactical.
- **Political-risk tails have widened.** Nikkei flags that a Trump impeachment push would "collapse" Democratic credibility [26], while Toyo Keizai examines whether Trump's "revenge" against opponents escalates after defeat [7]. Nikkei also sees a cornered Trump pivoting to diplomacy with China, Russia and North Korea as domestic policy stalls [29]. A US–China thaw would help Japanese exporters' China-exposed earnings (FA, machinery). An unpredictable approach to North Korea, however, raises a security premium for Japan.
- **Vance has broken with Trump over Iran.** He attributed the loss to "war," opening a flashpoint with Trump over Iran policy [18]. This is the first visible intra-party rift on the Middle East and feeds directly into oil (see Energy). It is a meaningful signal for the 2028 succession race and Republican foreign-policy direction.
- **Tokyo is set for a rebound.** Nikkei's pre-market preview expects buying aimed at an autonomous rebound after the US political shock [14]. Yahoo frames the midterms' impact on Japan through tariffs, yen and AI capex [38]. For context, the record one-day point drop was 4,451 yen on 5 August 2024, which was followed by a near-full rebound within days. A 3,000+ yen fall ranks among the largest point declines ever. Expect a sharp bounce in oversold large caps, but the AI-regulation overhang will cap tech-led recovery.

## AI, Data Centers & Semiconductors

- **AI-regulation fears drove the Nikkei crash.** Toyo Keizai asks whether the fear is an overreaction. It identifies a "hole in circulating funds" as the real vulnerability: hyperscaler and neocloud capex financed by recycled equity and credit flows that can reverse quickly [1][55]. This is the first major test of the AI-capex financing loop. Advantest, Tokyo Electron, SoftBank Group, Fujikura and Furukawa Electric carry the most index weight and crowding. Reduce sizing in names priced for uninterrupted capex growth.
- **Data-center opposition is spreading.** Opposition candidates won in Texas on platforms to brake AI data-center construction, and the movement is spreading across the US over power, water and grid costs [17]. The constraint is shifting from chips to permits and power. That is negative for pure data-center plays. It is relatively neutral to positive for Japanese grid-equipment makers (Hitachi Energy, Mitsubishi Electric, Fuji Electric), since utilities still need upgrades.
- **The AI boom is likely intact despite the CoreWeave shock.** Mainichi argues investment will continue despite CoreWeave's collapse in sentiment, because hyperscaler balance sheets remain strong [16]. CoreWeave is the bellwether for leveraged GPU clouds, which suggests stress is concentrated in credit-funded second-tier players rather than Microsoft, Google or Meta. Favour suppliers whose order books are tied to top-tier hyperscalers over those exposed to neoclouds.
- **The Kyushu semiconductor cluster keeps deepening.** Mitsubishi UFJ, Kikuyo Town and partners plan a joint semiconductor campus in Kumamoto adjacent to TSMC/JASM [21]. This continues the multi-year Kyushu "Silicon Island" build-out, supporting regional banks (Kyushu FG, Fukuoka FG), local real estate and construction. It is a structural trend, not a one-off.
- **Semiconductor-materials consolidation is accelerating.** Mitsui Chemicals' acquisition of JSR, the photoresist leader taken private by JIC in 2024 for roughly ¥900bn, signals JIC's exit path and Japan's push to build scale champions in materials [71][73]. Further consolidation is plausible among resist, wafer and specialty-gas players (Tokyo Ohka, Sumitomo Chemical, Resonac).
- **Qualcomm's numbers are a weak handset read-through.** FY sales fell 3% to $43.1bn and operating income dropped 30% to $8.65bn, though the dividend was raised to $3.62 [63]. The profit contraction reflects lost Apple modem share and soft handsets. That is mildly negative for Japanese smartphone-component suppliers (Murata, TDK, Taiyo Yuden). Auto and IoT diversification remains the offset.
- **Subsea cable investment is a secular theme.** Sumitomo Electric opened a European submarine cable base and Scottish factory [24]. Subsea cable demand from offshore wind interconnects and data links is strong. This diversifies Sumitomo Electric away from autos and is less exposed to US data-center permitting risk.
- **Vacuum technology remains a niche to watch.** Nikkan Kogyo's VACUUM 2026 preview highlights vacuum technology for chip and display tools [25]. Relevant names are ULVAC and Shimadzu.

## Energy & Commodities

- **WTI fell below $90 on hopes of Iran negotiations** after Vance's remarks [72]. This remains well above the $60–75 range of 2025, implying a sizeable geopolitical premium could unwind if talks progress. Lower oil helps Japan's terms of trade and trade balance, which is yen-supportive. It also helps airlines (ANA, JAL), chemicals and utilities' fuel costs. It is negative for INPEX and refiners' inventory valuation (ENEOS, Idemitsu).
- **Resources still lifted the trading houses.** Four trading houses guided higher for FY3/27 on resource prices [75]. A retreat in oil from elevated levels would compress upside to these guidances in H2. The shareholder-return story is less commodity-sensitive than the earnings story.
- **Bitcoin rebounded to the $80,000 level**, with Trump reported buying back after the defeat [19]. It remains well below the roughly $126k peak of October 2025, so crypto risk appetite is recovering, not euphoric. Relevant Japanese proxies are Metaplanet, Monex and the SBI group.

## Trade & Geopolitics

- **China is escalating anti-Japan diplomacy.** Wang Yi convened Mekong foreign ministers under a banner of "not tolerating Japanese militarism" while expanding AI and digital cooperation [36]. This continues the deterioration in China–Japan relations. China is actively courting ASEAN, which is relevant for a Malaysian investor watching regional supply-chain allegiances. It points to risk for Japanese consumer brands in China (Shiseido, Fast Retailing, Asahi). It supports defence names (Mitsubishi Heavy, Kawasaki Heavy, IHI).
- **The US political shift is a risk for Nippon Steel.** More than 40% of Nippon Steel's July–September profit outlook comes from US Steel [70]. The June 2025 acquisition, around $14bn with a US government "golden share," now faces a Democratic-controlled House allied with the steelworkers union, raising oversight and investment-commitment scrutiny. Nippon Steel has become a US-political-risk stock. Size accordingly ahead of its results.
- **A Trump tilt toward China, Russia and North Korea is double-edged for Japan** [29]. Tariff relief through US–China deals would help Japanese industrials. Any US–North Korea deal that bypasses Tokyo would be a security negative and supportive of defence-budget expansion.

## Japan Macro, Fiscal & Demographics

- **Births rose for the first time in 11 years.** Japanese births rose 0.4% to about 320,000 in H1 2026 [42]. This is notable given 2026 is a hinoeuma ("fire horse") year; in 1966, births fell roughly 25% on superstition. Calendar-year 2024 births were a record low of about 686,000. One half-year uptick is not a trend reversal, but it modestly tempers the demographic-decline narrative. It could support childcare, baby and education names (Pigeon, JP Holdings, Benesse) if sustained.
- **The food consumption-tax cut is leaking into savings.** A survey finds 25.7% of people will save the benefits of the food tax cut [45]. That dilutes the consumption multiplier, consistent with persistent precautionary saving. Temper expectations for a broad-based supermarket and food-retail volume boost. Discounters and drugstores (PPIH, Kobe Bussan, Welcia) remain best positioned.
- **The fiscal debate is intensifying.** Diamond notes consumption-tax revenue has risen more than fivefold since its 1989 introduction while national debt keeps swelling, and analyses the structural cause [54]. Combined with food-tax cuts, this feeds JGB supply and term-premium concerns. Super-long JGB yields remain the key fiscal-risk gauge. Higher long yields benefit life insurers (Dai-ichi Life, T&D) and banks, and hurt REITs and utilities' valuations.
- **Regional businesses are pressing for stimulus.** The Wakayama chamber federation filed 11 economic-measure requests with the prefecture [20]. This reflects SME cost pressure from wages and energy, consistent with nationwide calls ahead of a supplementary budget.
- **Cosmetic-medicine oversight is tightening.** A council proposed collecting fees from cosmetic medical institutions and redeploying local medical personnel [43]. Toyo Keizai's legal series on botched cosmetic surgery highlights rising litigation risk in the sector [51][52]. Regulatory tightening is a headwind for cosmetic-clinic operators and the platforms that advertise them.

## Banks, Brokers & Financials

- **Japan Post Bank is taking 20% of Matsui Securities** [34]. This is a major entry into online brokerage as the new NISA drives retail investment flows, giving Japan Post Bank's huge deposit base a distribution channel. Matsui gains a strategic backer and potential re-rating. It raises competitive pressure on SBI, Rakuten and Monex in a zero-commission market. It also signals Japan Post Bank's continued shift from JGB-heavy assets toward fee income.
- **The FSA has inspected Sony Financial Group on site** [37]. Sony FG was spun off and relisted in September 2025. Scrutiny of a newly independent insurer, bank and asset manager adds near-term headline risk. Watch for findings on governance or product sales.
- **US financial optimism needs caution.** Nikkei warns against extrapolating US bank strength after the Democratic win [15]. Japanese megabanks rest more on domestic rate normalisation and NIM expansion than on US deregulation, so that thesis is unaffected.

## Infrastructure, Real Estate & Regional Development

- **JR Central may raise Linear costs again.** It is considering another increase in Chuo Shinkansen (maglev) construction costs [32]. The estimate was previously raised to about ¥7trn in 2021 from ¥5.5trn, and the Tokyo–Nagoya opening has already slipped beyond 2027 over Shizuoka delays. Further overruns pressure JR Central's balance sheet and dividend capacity, but benefit general contractors (Obayashi, Kajima, Taisei, Shimizu).
- **Fukuoka's hotel boom continues.** Successive hotel openings and renewals emphasise "experiential value" [22]. This reflects inbound tourism strength and Fukuoka's position as Japan's fastest-growing major city. Positive for hotel REITs and regional developers (Nishi-Nippon Railroad, Kyushu Railway).
- **Seibu is pursuing regional revitalisation.** Seibu Railway joined 11 local governments along the Shinjuku Line in a regional revitalisation council [40]. It supports Seibu HD's real estate-led strategy and line-side value creation.
- **Rakumachi landlord columns** promote real-estate investment [31][39]. These reflect continued retail appetite for property despite rising rates, but carry no direct market signal.

## Consumer, Food Service & Entertainment

- **Sushi restaurant failures have surged to a 25-year high** in closures and bankruptcies [41]. Rising fish, rice and labour costs are squeezing independents. This is a consolidation tailwind for scale chains (FOOD & LIFE COMPANIES/Sushiro, Kura Sushi, Zensho), which can absorb costs.
- **Inbound tourism is now reaching regional Japan.** Sanuki udon restaurants in Kagawa are struggling with crowds [35]. This supports Toridoll (Marugame Seimen) and regional rail and transport operators.
- **McDonald's Japan is helping offset US weakness.** McDonald's July–September profit rose 9%, with Japan and Europe offsetting slowing US traffic [64]. This confirms McDonald's Holdings Japan (2702) as a structural winner on pricing power and value perception.
- **Cybersecurity is spreading to mid-size consumer firms.** After unauthorised access, Yudetaro abolished its membership system rather than hold personal data [23]. This follows a string of Japanese cyber incidents and supports demand for security vendors (Trend Micro, LAC, Digital Arts).
- **Toho's IP franchise is firing.** "Godzilla -0.0" opened above its predecessor and is tipped to top ¥10bn at the box office [53]. "Godzilla Minus One," the 2023 Oscar winner, set the benchmark. This is a direct earnings driver for Toho and supports the Japanese content-export thesis.

## Corporate Governance & Business Features

- **GMO's founder exposed governance concerns at an apology press conference.** Toyo Keizai details founder Masatoshi Kumagai's "me-first, micro-control" style, including his boast that GMO would become "the Mitsubishi Group" [8][9]. Key-man and governance risk is a discount factor across the GMO listed group: GMO Internet Group, GMO Payment Gateway, GMO Financial HD and GMO Internet.
- **Locondo's aggressive M&A carries integration risk.** Under President Yusuke Tanaka, Locondo is pursuing roughly ¥10bn per year of acquisitions [56]. Shareholder-dialogue and execution risks are high for this small-cap roll-up.
- **NTT has disclosed its pay structure.** Diamond reveals managers earn ¥18.4–20m, more 30-somethings are being promoted to manager, and an AI-driven transfer system is being introduced [5]. This shows Japan Inc.'s shift away from seniority pay, which supports productivity narratives but adds to structural wage inflation.
- **Other features carry no direct investment signal.** These cover Tesla's Roadster commercial viability [4], social media missteps around new Giants manager Hideki Matsui's greeting video (Yomiuri, unlisted) [6], marriage-hunting and lifestyle pieces [2][3], a Tokyo film festival award [44], a UNESCO recommendation for Japanese calligraphy [30], and a Battle of Leyte Gulf memorial op-ed [11].

## Company Briefs

- **Earnings & guidance:**
  - **Trading houses:** Four majors guided higher for FY3/27 on resources [75]. Mitsubishi Corp, Itochu and IHI made Kabutan's positive-results list [46].
  - **Kyushu Electric:** Raised its full-year net profit forecast to ¥140bn on nuclear utilisation and fuel-cost tailwinds [67].
  - **Saibu Gas:** Raised its final profit forecast [68].
  - **TOTO:** Interim net profit rose 2.4x, signalling recovery after restructuring and China weakness [69].
  - **Zenrin:** Swung to an interim loss on higher investment costs [65].
  - **Crafteia:** Posted record interim profit [66].
  - **Ocean Network Express (ONE):** Raised its FY net profit forecast to $2bn from $900m. That is a direct equity-method boost for NYK, MOL and Kawasaki Kisen, which own roughly 38/31/31% [48].
  - **Rasa Industries:** Weak on profit-taking despite a guidance raise, a sign of "sell the news" in crowded semi-adjacent small caps [49].
  - **Other strong reporters:** AREHD, Rasa and Astellas flagged as post-close standouts [50]. Chiyoken, Krasil and Gurunavi lead among Standard/Growth names [47].
  - **Nippon Steel:** More than 40% of profits from US Steel heading into results [70].
  - **Qualcomm:** Sales down 3%, operating income down 30%, dividend raised [63].
  - **McDonald's:** Profit up 9% on Japan strength [64].
- **Capital returns:**
  - **Mitsubishi Corp:** ¥1trn share buyback, matching the scale of last year's programme under Corporate Strategy 2027 [75].
  - **Buyback screen:** Kabutan lists buybacks announced after the 4 November close, a useful screen given the Nikkei drawdown [62].
  - **High-yield screen:** Kabutan's top-30 high-dividend undervalued screen [74].
- **M&A & strategic stakes:**
  - **Mitsui Chemicals–JSR:** Large semiconductor-materials acquisition. The market warns of balance-sheet deterioration, so expect leverage and rating scrutiny and pressure on Mitsui Chemicals shares [71][73].
  - **Japan Post Bank–Matsui Securities:** Japan Post Bank acquires 20% of Matsui, a positive re-rating catalyst for Matsui [34].
  - **Locondo:** Serial M&A at about ¥10bn per year [56].
- **Regulatory & governance:**
  - **Sony FG:** FSA on-site inspection [37].
  - **GMO group:** Founder governance concerns surfaced at an apology press conference [8][9].
  - **Yudetaro:** Scrapped its membership system after a data breach [23].
- **Single-stock moves:**
  - **Nissan:** Shares hit the lowest level in half a century, below post-Lehman lows. Nissan risks sliding toward "small-cap" status and index-weight downgrades. Restructuring execution remains the only catalyst [27].
- **IPO:**
  - **LTV-X (655A):** Debuts on the Nagoya Stock Exchange Next market with buy orders exceeding supply at the open [57].
- **Capex & operations:**
  - **Sumitomo Electric:** European subsea cable base and Scottish factory [24].
  - **MUFG:** Kumamoto semiconductor campus [21].
  - **Toho:** Godzilla box-office strength [53].
  - **JR Central:** Linear cost overrun risk [32].

## What to Watch
